capability.conversionCommand: qemu-img convert -p -O qcow2 '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.img' '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2'
capability.detail: Veil's default system disk is raw, and QEMU internal snapshots can only be stored inside a qcow2 image. Suspend and resume still work on this disk because they stream guest memory to a separate file.

nextActions: Veil's default system disk is raw, and QEMU internal snapshots can only be stored inside a qcow2 image. Suspend and resume still work on this disk because they stream guest memory to a separate file.
Convert the system disk with: qemu-img convert -p -O qcow2 '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.img' '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2'
Then point the VM profile's virtual disk at /Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2 and keep the original file until Windows boots from the converted disk.
Use veil-vmctl vm-suspend --json when you only need to keep the current Windows session, which works on the current disk format.
